19 What is a unit for stress?
A
kg m–1
s–2
B
kg m–2
s–2
C
N m–1
D
N m

hints: Start from what stress means: force acting per unit cross-sectional area of the stretched material.
Write that relationship as units: newton divided by metre squared, $\text{N m}^{-2}$.
Expand $1 \text{ N} = 1 \text{ kg m s}^{-2}$ and divide by $\text{m}^{2}$ to find the base-unit power of $\text{m}$.
walkthrough: Recall the definition of tensile stress: $stress = F/A$, where $F$ is force and $A$ is cross-sectional area.
Therefore the unit of stress is the unit of force divided by the unit of area: $\text{N m}^{-2}$, also called the pascal.
Write the newton in SI base units using $F = ma$: $1 \text{ N} = 1 \text{ kg m s}^{-2}$.
Divide by $\text{m}^{2}$: $\text{N m}^{-2} = (\text{kg m s}^{-2}) / \text{m}^{2} = \text{kg m}^{-1}\text{s}^{-2}$.
This matches $\text{kg m}^{-1}\text{s}^{-2}$. This is option A.

A.explanation: Stress has units of force per area, and $\text{kg m}^{-1}\text{s}^{-2}$ is equivalent to $\text{N m}^{-2}$ or pascal.

B.explanation: This has an extra $\text{m}^{-1}$ factor and corresponds to force divided by volume, not force divided by area.

C.explanation: $\text{N m}^{-1}$ is force per length, for example spring constant or surface tension, not force per area.

D.explanation: $\text{N m}$ is force times distance, for example moment or energy, not force divided by area.
